summary: Strontium niobate thin films were deposited using atomic layer deposition (ALD) to explore their potential as high-k dielectrics. The super-cycle method was used to control the composition of the films, and the dielectric properties were evaluated. Sr-rich films showed high dielectric constants, while Nb-rich films exhibited amorphous structures with moderate dielectric constants.
evidence: Strontium niobate thin films have potential for next-generation high-k dielectric applications. In this work, we investigated the fabrication of Sr xNb1-xOy thin films by atomic layer deposition for the first time and examined their physical and electrical characteristics. The Sr-rich film was crystalline after annealing and showed a high dielectric constant of approximately 75. In addition, it was observed that the Nb-rich film had a relatively large dielectric constant of approximately 65 even though it was amorphous, confirming that it could be applied as a next-generation high-k material.
